text: Flipped every production SQLite database from the default rollback journal to WAL mode via PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; concurrent readers no longer block the writer, which is the whole reason we bothered.

queries.text: which SQLite journaling mode replaced the rollback journal in production and which pragma flipped it
sqlite wal journal mode pragma rollback concurrent reader writer

text: Lowered PRAGMA synchronous from FULL to NORMAL on the analytics replica after measuring a 3x commit speedup; durability is still safe enough because WAL mode only loses uncommitted transactions on a power cut.

queries.text: which synchronous level replaced FULL on the analytics replica and why was the durability trade acceptable
sqlite pragma synchronous full normal wal commit speed durability

text: PRAGMA foreign_keys defaults off in SQLite for backward compatibility, so every connection opener in the service now runs it as ON right after connect; orphan rows stopped appearing in the audit table within a day.

queries.text: which per-connection pragma stopped orphan rows in the audit table and why is it off by default
sqlite pragma foreign keys orphan audit connection default off

text: Bumped PRAGMA cache_size to -65536 to let SQLite hold roughly 64 MB of pages per connection in memory; the large reporting query that used to chew disk now stays entirely in the page cache.

queries.text: which pragma expanded the per-connection page cache to about 64 MB and what query benefited
sqlite pragma cache size page reporting query memory connection

text: Turned on PRAGMA mmap_size=268435456 for the read-mostly replica so SQLite memory-maps up to 256 MB of the database file; random reads drop under the syscall threshold and the kernel page cache does the rest.

queries.text: which SQLite pragma memory-maps up to 256 MB of the database file on the read replica
sqlite pragma mmap size memory map replica kernel cache random

text: Ripped shared-cache mode out of the SQLite connection opener after an upstream warning that it is deprecated and error-prone; each connection now owns its cache and the intermittent SQLITE_LOCKED under load disappeared.

queries.text: which deprecated SQLite feature was removed after locking errors under load and what replaced it
sqlite shared cache deprecate locked connection own private

text: Switched the hot-path lookup tables to WITHOUT ROWID; SQLite stores them as a clustered index on the primary key rather than a rowid heap with a secondary index, and point lookups dropped by roughly a third.

queries.text: which SQLite table flavour replaced rowid tables on hot-path lookups and what storage shape does it use
sqlite without rowid clustered index primary key hot lookup

text: Adopted SQLite FTS5 virtual tables for the product search index; the earlier LIKE scan on the description column stopped scaling past about fifty thousand rows and the tokenizer unicode61 folded diacritics for free.

queries.text: which SQLite extension replaced a LIKE scan for product search and which tokenizer handled diacritics
sqlite fts5 virtual table like scan unicode61 tokenizer diacritic

text: The FTS5 BM25 ranker sorts search results without a second trip through the main table; the built-in bm25() function takes the virtual-table row and returns a score we feed straight into the ORDER BY.

queries.text: which ranking function does FTS5 expose for ordering matches and where does it plug into the query
fts5 bm25 rank function virtual table order by score sqlite

text: The office espresso machine was making a new rattling sound this morning and nobody is willing to open the panel to investigate.

Added the spellfix1 extension alongside FTS5 so typo-tolerant lookups fall back to edit-distance candidates; the product catalogue now returns results for queries like 'headphnes' that used to come back empty.

queries.text: which SQLite extension adds typo-tolerant fallback to FTS5 and what algorithm powers the candidates
sqlite spellfix1 fts5 edit distance typo tolerant fallback product

text: SQLite R-Tree virtual tables drive the 'stores near me' query; a bounding-box prefilter on latitude and longitude pairs narrows the candidate set before the haversine sort, and p99 dropped under 20 ms.

queries.text: which spatial virtual table prefilters the stores-near-me query before the haversine sort
sqlite r tree virtual table bounding box haversine latitude longitude

text: Imported the legacy CSV dumps with the SQLite CSV virtual table so we can SELECT against the file directly without a load step; a one-off migration used it to reconcile two years of invoices in an hour.

queries.text: which SQLite virtual table let us SELECT against raw CSV without a load step during invoice reconciliation
sqlite csv virtual table select file load migration invoice

text: The JSON1 extension is now the only JSON path; every code path uses json_extract, json_each, and json_group_array instead of parsing strings in the application layer after pulling blobs out.

queries.text: which SQLite extension replaced application-side JSON parsing and which three operators cover most queries
sqlite json1 json extract each group array application parse

text: Series virtual table generate_series(1, 1000) fills the calendar-dim table without a host-side loop; a recursive CTE used to do the same job but the virtual table keeps the schema migration single-statement.

queries.text: which SQLite virtual table fills calendar-dim rows and what did it replace in the migration
sqlite generate series virtual table recursive cte calendar migration

text: Generated columns on the orders table materialise tax and total from the base line items; STORED generated columns get indexed like any normal column, so the reporting view no longer recomputes on every read.

queries.text: which SQLite feature materialises tax and total columns so reports stop recomputing on every read
sqlite generated column stored indexed orders tax total report

text: Rolled the reporting dashboards onto SQLite window functions; ROW_NUMBER, LAG, and SUM OVER replaced a nest of correlated subqueries and the quarterly comparison query runs in sub-second time.

queries.text: which SQL feature replaced correlated subqueries on the reporting dashboards and which window operators matter most
sqlite window function row number lag sum over correlated subquery

text: The org-chart traversal uses WITH RECURSIVE on a parent_id column; SQLite's common-table-expression (CTE) support handles the closure walk without a stored procedure, which we would not have had anyway.

queries.text: which SQL construct walks the org-chart closure in SQLite without relying on a stored procedure
sqlite with recursive cte parent id org chart closure walk

text: Migrated SQLite schema definitions to STRICT tables on the new service; the type affinity footgun where inserting 'abc' into an INTEGER column silently stored a TEXT value is now a hard error instead of a surprise.

queries.text: which SQLite table mode replaced type-affinity laxness and what class of silent bug did it retire
sqlite strict table type affinity integer text silent bug

text: The SQLite RETURNING clause dropped a round trip on every order insert; the INSERT now returns the generated id and timestamp in the same statement, replacing a follow-up SELECT last_insert_rowid() call.

queries.text: which SQLite clause dropped a second round trip after INSERT and what did it replace
sqlite returning clause insert last insert rowid round trip

text: SQLite ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is the upsert pattern on the user-settings table; matching on the unique key either inserts the row or bumps updated_at, and the application no longer needs a SELECT-then-branch.

queries.text: which SQLite upsert pattern replaced the select-then-branch on user settings
sqlite on conflict do update upsert user settings unique

text: AFTER UPDATE triggers sync the audit_log table whenever a row in accounts changes; the trigger body writes the old and new JSON blobs with json_object so downstream consumers always see the diff.

queries.text: which trigger populates the audit log on account changes and how are old and new values captured
sqlite after update trigger audit log accounts json object

text: Adopted SQLCipher for the on-device store on the mobile client; transparent AES-256 page encryption replaced our previous app-layer field encryption and key rotation is now a single PRAGMA rekey call.

queries.text: which encryption layer replaced app-level field encryption on the mobile store and how does key rotation work
sqlcipher aes 256 pragma rekey field encryption mobile rotate

text: Litestream streams WAL segments to S3 continuously from the edge VPS; a crash-restart on the primary rehydrates from the last WAL segment and the RPO is measured in single-digit seconds.

queries.text: which tool streams SQLite WAL segments to S3 and what is the recovery-point objective it achieves
litestream sqlite wal s3 edge vps rpo replication stream

text: Moved multi-region reads to LiteFS on Fly.io; the FUSE-backed distributed file system gives every region a read replica of the SQLite file, and write forwarding to the primary is handled in-process.

queries.text: which distributed file system gave multi-region SQLite reads on Fly.io and how does it surface replicas
litefs fly io fuse sqlite multi region replica write forward

text: Simon Willison's sqlite-utils is the default CLI for ad-hoc work; piping JSON into sqlite-utils insert creates the schema, indexes a column, and returns a queryable file in one shell command.

queries.text: which CLI do we reach for on ad-hoc SQLite work and who wrote it
sqlite utils cli simon willison json insert schema ad hoc

text: sqlite-web gets launched against the prod replica when a support engineer needs to poke at rows; the tiny Flask UI beats installing a desktop GUI client and the replica is read-only so nothing gets clobbered.

queries.text: which tool lets support engineers browse the prod replica without a desktop GUI
sqlite web flask prod replica read only support browser

text: Published the open-data snapshots through Datasette; Simon Willison's publish command wraps the database in a read-only JSON API with facets, which means the frontend team stopped asking for bespoke endpoints.

queries.text: which tool turns a SQLite file into a read-only JSON API with facets and who authored it
datasette simon willison json api facet read only snapshot

text: iOS Core Data still runs on top of SQLite under the hood; dropping to raw FMDB for the bulk-import path was cheaper than fighting managed-object-context merge conflicts on 50k rows.

queries.text: which iOS persistence path dropped under Core Data for bulk import and what is its backing store
ios core data sqlite fmdb bulk import managed object context

text: Android Room generates the SQLite schema and DAO code at compile time; the @Query annotations get validated against the actual schema, which caught two drift bugs before they shipped.

queries.text: which Android library validates SQL against the actual SQLite schema at compile time
android room sqlite dao query annotation compile schema drift

text: Picked DuckDB over SQLite for the analytics-only service; columnar storage, vectorised execution, and native Parquet reads demolished the row-based scan path on our six-way joins.

queries.text: which embedded OLAP engine replaced SQLite for the analytics service and what made the difference
duckdb sqlite parquet columnar vectorised analytics join scan

text: The embedded KV under the indexer moved from SQLite to libmdbx after the B-tree page-split pattern on monotonically-increasing keys spiked write amplification; mdbx copy-on-write pages behaved better.

queries.text: which embedded KV replaced SQLite under the indexer and what B-tree pathology forced the swap
libmdbx sqlite b tree page split write amplification copy on write

text: LMDB powers the session cache in the gateway; memory-mapped reads with zero-copy keys meant the hot path bypasses the user-space allocator entirely, and p99 on session lookup sits under 50 microseconds.

queries.text: which embedded database backs the gateway session cache and what latency does the memory map deliver
lmdb session cache gateway memory map zero copy p99 microsecond

text: RocksDB sits under the write-heavy event store; LSM compaction copes with the append rate where a B-tree engine would have been buried, and tiered compression keeps disk spend flat.

queries.text: which embedded engine underpins the event store and what compaction model does it use
rocksdb lsm b tree event store compaction append write heavy

text: Sled was fun to prototype against but we dropped it for the durable pipeline; the project maintainer explicitly flagged it as beta and the sister project Fjall is taking the LSM torch forward.

queries.text: which Rust embedded database replaced Sled for the durable pipeline after a beta-status warning
sled fjall rust embedded lsm beta durable pipeline

text: Rust services use rusqlite for the SQLite bindings; compile-time prepared statements via the include_str! macro mean a typo in SQL fails the build, not a 3 a.m. pager.

queries.text: which Rust SQLite binding catches SQL typos at build time and which macro loads the query
rusqlite rust sqlite include str compile time prepared statement

text: better-sqlite3 is the Node.js binding to SQLite on the CLI tools; the synchronous API is the right call there because there is no event loop to starve and the numbers on bulk insert clobber async bindings.

queries.text: which synchronous Node binding powers the CLI tools and why is the sync API correct there
better sqlite3 node cli synchronous api bulk insert event loop

text: sqlx in its offline mode ships a cached schema so the Rust service compiles without a live database; the build step runs cargo sqlx prepare against a dev SQLite file and commits the JSON cache.

queries.text: which Rust query crate supports an offline schema cache and what command populates it
sqlx rust sqlite offline cargo prepare schema cache compile

text: Python async services use aiosqlite on the IO boundary; the thread-pool executor under the hood is a compromise because libsqlite3 is synchronous, but the async surface stays consistent with the rest of asyncio.

queries.text: which Python library gives an async surface over the synchronous libsqlite3 and what is under the hood
aiosqlite python asyncio libsqlite3 thread pool async surface

text: Swapped the stdlib sqlite3 module for pysqlite3 on the analytics workers because the shipped Python was pinned to an old SQLite build without JSON1 or window functions support; pysqlite3-binary carries a newer library.

queries.text: which Python module replaced stdlib sqlite3 on workers and what features were missing from the bundled build
pysqlite3 stdlib python json1 window function analytics worker

text: SQLite itself is maintained by D. Richard Hipp and the SQLite consortium; the codebase has the TH3 test harness with branch coverage over 100 percent, which is why we trust a file-shaped database in production.

queries.text: who maintains SQLite and which proprietary test harness gives it over 100 percent branch coverage
sqlite richard hipp consortium th3 test harness branch coverage

text: Richard Hipp originally wrote SQLite in 2000 for a US Navy project on General Dynamics guided-missile destroyers; that origin story is in the official documentation and is why the public-domain license still holds.

queries.text: which 2000 Navy project birthed SQLite and which license choice dates to that origin
sqlite richard hipp us navy general dynamics public domain 2000

text: Someone left a birthday cake in the kitchen with no name on the card and the third-floor team is in a standoff about whether it is polite to cut it.

Reference the PRAGMA journal_mode documentation when onboarding new engineers; the page enumerates DELETE, TRUNCATE, PERSIST, MEMORY, WAL, and OFF with the trade-offs of each, and the WAL section links out to the WAL2 future-work notes.

queries.text: which SQLite doc page covers the journal-mode options and how they trade off durability
sqlite pragma journal mode delete truncate persist memory wal off

text: Keep the FTS5 contentless-table trick in the playbook; declaring content='' tells SQLite to skip storing the indexed text, and we point the BM25 ranker at the primary orders table via an external-content FTS index.

queries.text: which FTS5 storage trick avoids duplicating indexed text while still supporting BM25 ranking
fts5 contentless external content bm25 orders index duplicate

text: Turned on SQLite PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY on the batch importer; temporary b-trees for ORDER BY and GROUP BY stay in RAM instead of spilling to the temp file, which cut the long aggregation runs by about 40 percent.

queries.text: which SQLite pragma keeps temporary b-trees in RAM and which clauses benefit most on the batch importer
sqlite pragma temp store memory order by group by aggregation

text: Shipped the first milestone of the offline-first mobile client: SQLite under SQLCipher on device, Litestream replicating to S3, and a LiteFS-backed primary on Fly.io tying the two ends together.

queries.text: which four-piece stack ties the offline-first mobile client to a Fly.io primary and S3 archive
offline mobile sqlite sqlcipher litestream litefs fly io s3

text: Landed the cross-database migration milestone: moved the analytics pipeline from SQLite to DuckDB while keeping SQLite for the OLTP service, with the same sqlite-utils import tooling feeding both engines.

queries.text: which dual-engine split landed with sqlite-utils feeding both the OLTP SQLite and the analytics DuckDB
sqlite duckdb sqlite utils analytics oltp pipeline migration

text: Published a reference runbook for SQLite corruption triage: first PRAGMA integrity_check, then PRAGMA quick_check, then .recover in the sqlite3 CLI, and only if all three fail do we restore from the last Litestream generation.

queries.text: which three-step corruption triage runs before we fall back to a Litestream restore
sqlite integrity check quick recover cli litestream corruption runbook

text: Preferred binding stack across services: rusqlite for Rust, better-sqlite3 for Node CLIs, aiosqlite for Python async, and sqlx for the Rust services that need compile-time query checking against a dev SQLite file.

queries.text: which SQLite bindings are preferred across Rust services, Node CLIs, and Python async code
rusqlite better sqlite3 aiosqlite sqlx binding preference rust node python
